thread:
Alex G: Heads-up — starting ~02:30 UTC we started seeing p95/p99 spikes for the acme-corp Dedicated pool (acme-prod). User reports and synthetic checks both show p99 jumping from ~600ms to 6-12s for short prompts.

oncall-bot: ALERT: High latency detected for pool acme-prod — p99 > 5s for 10m (alert #SRE-4521)

Maria P: I see the same in the telemetry. Heatmap shows a tight cluster of short requests that suddenly get queued. Resource graphs show GPUs scaled down around 01:58 UTC, then a slow ramp back up.

Josh R: Any recent rollout to autoscaler or pool config?

Priya I: We rolled the new autoscaler config yesterday (rm: disable-aggressive-min). Looks like min_capacity for acme-prod got lowered to 1 during the rollout and cooldown was left at 600s. That combo + instance boot time ~= 3-5m explains scale-up lag and cold GPU starts.

Alex G: Can someone pull the autoscaler logs? I want the timeline: scale-down, incoming burst, scale-up attempts, errors.

Priya I: pasted logs:

```
2026-03-15T01:58:04Z autoscaler[acme-prod]: scaling down from 6 -> 1 (min_capacity=1)
2026-03-15T02:28:10Z autoscaler[acme-prod]: pending_queue_len=120, predicted_needed=5, action=scale_up -> launch request sent
2026-03-15T02:28:12Z infra-orch: launch-gpu-instance request accepted instance_request_id=ir_9a7
2026-03-15T02:31:35Z infra-orch: instance ir_9a7 -> ready
2026-03-15T02:31:40Z serving-runtime: warmup started for instance ir_9a7
2026-03-15T02:32:12Z serving-runtime: instance warm -> healthy
```

Priya I: So ~4 mins between launch request and instance warm. Meanwhile queue built up and p99 spiked.

Lina (support): Customer (acme) called — they're hit by elevated latency in production and noticed errors when requests timed out after 15s. They want ETA and what went wrong.

Josh R: Repro steps for us to measure: run 200 concurrent short requests (prompt length 10 tokens) against dedicated endpoint. Example: 

```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood/infer" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"acme-prod-v3","prompt":"hi","max_tokens":10}' &
done; wait
```

Josh R: In local run saw p50=450ms p95=1.2s p99=9.8s when pool had scaled down.

Alex G: Short-term mitigation: can we manually scale the pool up to absorb current load and reduce cold starts? Also consider routing acme's small requests to hosted fallback while we fix autoscaler config.

Priya I: I can manual scale now. Command: `rwdctl dedicated scale --pool acme-prod --count 8 --reason "emergency p99 mitigation"`

Priya I: Done — scaled to 8. Observability shows p99 dropping from ~9s to ~1.1s in ~2m after warmup completes.

Maria P: Good. Next step: revert the min_capacity change for critical customers — set min_capacity=3 for acme-prod and add burst_pool=2 prewarmed instances. Also reduce cooldown for scale-up for critical pools from 600s -> 60s so we don't block subsequent launches during surges.

Alex G: We should also add a safety rule: if pending queue > 80 for >30s, bypass cooldown and launch immediately. That would have prevented the long tail here.

Josh R: For post-incident: need clear repro artifacts. I stored the curl run results and histograms in /tmp/acme-latency-20260315.json and uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-debug/acme/2026-03-15-latency.json

Lina (support): I'll update customer: "We identified autoscaler config change that reduced minimum capacity overnight which, combined with cooldown settings, caused scale-up lag. We've manually scaled the pool and are applying config changes; we expect normal latency within minutes. We'll follow up with root cause and fix timeline."

Priya I: Action items I'm doing now: 1) apply min_capacity=3 and burst_pool=2 for acme-prod (in progress), 2) change cooldown override for critical pools, 3) create prewarm job that keeps burst_pool instances warm, 4) add alert rule to detect aggressive scale-down in last 12h.

Maria P: I'll open PR to revert the rollout that lowered min_capacity globally and add a gating test to block lower-than-recommended min for pools with SLA tags. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/autoscaler/pulls/842

Alex G: Who owns customer follow-up? Lina? Also we need runbook updates for oncall so scale-down rollouts are safer.

Lina (support): I will send the customer update now and cc SRE.

Alex G: Assign owners: Priya -> infra changes & prewarm, Maria -> PR + rollout blocker, Josh -> repro artifact and perf test harness updates, Lina -> customer comms. We'll reconvene in 30m and close once metrics stable for 1h.

sre-bot: NOTE: creating incident ticket SRE-4521 and attaching autoscaler logs.

oncall-bot: Reminder: follow the dedicated pool emergency checklist when scaling manually: `rwdctl` commands, tag changes, and telemetry sampling.

Alex G: Post-mortem draft later: root cause = autoscaler rollout that allowed dangerous min_capacity and a cooldown logic that didn't consider pending queue size; contributing factor = lack of warm-burst pool for critical customers. Proposed long-term fixes: prewarm pools for SLA customers, cooldown bypass for critical queue pressure, rollout gating tests, and a canary that simulates sudden short-request spikes.

Priya I: I'll also instrument instance boot time metrics at finer granularity (infra-orch -> instance_boot_latency) so we can predict effective scale-up delay per cloud region.

Maria P: Putting tentative ETA: infra changes + PR merged by EOD, prewarm job next week, runbook updated today.

Lina (support): Customer update sent: "We scaled your Dedicated pool and applied configuration to prevent recurrence. We'll share a full RCA within 48 hours."

Alex G: Closing this thread once last_message_ts shows steady metrics. Thanks everyone.
